author: Ryan Burge
title: You Know What You Need for Christmas? Graphs about Religion
original_title: You Know What You Need for Christmas? Graphs about Religion
summary: And I have a discount that is just for you!
full_content:
Hey Team-

It’s been another tremendous year at this weird little newsletter. Who would have thought that making hundreds of graphs about religion would end up being all of this? Certainly not me.

But you guys keep reading and I just keep on writing. And that’s just a gift that I will never take for granted.

A few months ago I was asked what motivates me to keep doing this 104 times a year and the answer for me is deeply personal — it keeps the darkness away. I need to work. I don’t do well with idle time and idle thoughts. I need to focus them on something that is positive. Some guys fish or play golf or have a lively fantasy football league. I do this.

I’ve added about 10,000 new free subscribers in the last 365 days. Actually 9,550 as of this writing. The year before that? 10,627. Not bad. And no real signs of a significant slowdown.

In the past year, these posts have been read nearly 3.3 million times. That’s the part that just boggles my mind. I will always publish most of my content for free initially.

And I’ve really tried to step my game up when it comes to rewarding my paid subscribers for their loyalty. Here are all the perks that you get:

  1. You can comment on the posts. This has made the discussion section so much better. And I love when someone pays me $6 for a one month subscription just to yell at me in the comments. That’s commitment.

  2. You have access to a huge archive. Like, a staggering amount of information. There are about 350 full-length pieces that are only accessible to paid subscribers now. That’s half a million words. I had AI build a really good search engine of all my posts, too. You can take that for a test drive here.

  3. I am adding a lot more interactive widgets to my posts that can only be accessed by paid subscribers. Just a few examples:

    1. A quiz next month that includes seventeen questions that will tell you how evangelical you are.

    2. An interactive map of over 8,000 ELCA congregations in the United States. You can click on any single point and see information like average worship attendance, their operating expenses and how many members they have.

    3. A widget that allows you to adjust parameters like the number of children in a denomination and what percentage will be retained into adulthood to generate an estimate of that denomination’s membership twenty years from now.

  4. And I’ve got some really unbelievable stuff on the horizon. Like a three part series on what is happening in the United Methodist Church (see below for a map prototype of churches that have disappeared from the UMC website). And then there’s a database that I’ve been assembling of every religious organization in the United States (which currently has over 700,000 entries). I don’t even know what I am going to do with that yet.

The hardest part of my job is to actually hold all that cool stuff back and not immediately post it on social media.

Are you enticed now to become a paid subscriber? Of course you are. So here’s the deal. Between now and December 31st you can become an annual subscriber to this newsletter for 20% off. That puts the price at $48 for all this graph-y goodness.

Take 20% Off Forever

And here’s the best part — this will renew at the same rate in perpetuity. So you can sign up today and get the same deal next year without having to cancel and renew and all that nonsense.

This would make a great gift for your pastor, too!

What about a ministry staff where everyone wants to read this newsletter? Well, if you can get at least three people to sign up from the same organization, I will knock the price down to just $40 per person.

A 33% Off Group Discount

One more thing before I close up. If you ever need to use something from this newsletter for your classroom syllabus or you are a small group leader at your church and want to send a specific post to all the members, just go ahead and do it. I obviously enjoy receiving compensation for my time and efforts. But I also want people to understand the world better and money shouldn’t stand in the way of that.

If you need a PDF of anything behind the paywall, just reach out and it’s all yours.

Thank you all, truly. Let’s do it again next year.

Ryan P. Burge is a professor of practice at the Danforth Center on Religion and Politics at Washington University.
rewritten_title: You Know What You Need for Christmas? Graphs about Religion
